correctness.rationale: Exact scalar minimization gives the two multipliers. Independence provides H^n. Strict convexity before the unique denominator pole and strict decrease afterwards prove two and only two crossings for all q>d>0. Maximizing the cross-to-Rayleigh quotient gives the exact inclusive angular frontier. The strong law and strict Jensen inequality establish an open almost-sure stable yet mean-square unstable interval; an exact rational witness and standalone checker verify critical identities. Nonunique minimizers are excluded.

Earlier abstract parabolic MinRes literature treats test compatibility and missing residual complements, generic independent-product theory treats moment versus pathwise stability, and operator-turning-angle theory treats the isolated angle optimization. None of the accessed formulations states this complete specialized phase diagram. A full later-section inspection of the motivating primary paper was unavailable, leaving explicit residual risk.

value.rationale: Random test-space resampling is a motivated idealized extension of finite-test residual minimization. The theorem provides a sharp angle/condition-number tolerance, identifies reentrant instability in step size, and separates typical convergence from diverging second moments while measured finite-test residuals remain zero. These identify a substantive diagnostics boundary, not a minor constant improvement or arbitrary parameter slice.
